task: round21 skeptic VALUE+FEASIBILITY of R21RK-4 (latency read rule for CI files)
reason: The core claim holds, and the rule costs nothing. It is a read rule, not a mechanism, so R8 does not apply. It only turns codes into '?' and never creates a '+', so it is conservative. I read exp79a cell 8 (experiments/exp79a_k2cap6_coordinject/exp79a-k2cap6-coordinject.ipynb). It confirms several EARLY no-op paths that add about 0 latency and leave submission.csv as exp70g wrote it: FORCE_FAIL, knobs out of range, SKIPPED (no GPU), dataset-not-found or sha mismatch in the outer try/except ('COORDINJECT FAILED ... unchanged'), and per-video WORKER FAILED on every video when each failure is fast ('no video was refined; submission.csv unchanged'). SKIPPED (deadline) needs kernel elapsed > 37,200 s, so L > 10.3 h, which is already a 'v' = '?'. The separation is real. K2-like latencies with insertion lie in 7.36-7.81 h (#37 7.54, exp70g 7.67, exp70q 7.81 = L_hi). A working CI adds about 2.0-2.9 h: t ~ 52 s + 0.00228 s/det, dets ~1.45x nodes, 100-130 hidden videos, 2 workers. So the +1.2 h line sits about 0.8 h below the CI lower bound and well above the ~0.3 h same-config noise. Three holes weaken the rule as written, but they do not refute it. (1) Latency is NECESSARY, not sufficient. LATE no-op paths spend the full CI time and then leave the CSV unchanged: an exception in coordinject_rewrite_csv (field-count ValueError, missing column, or MemoryError, since the main process loads ALL video npz into `refined` plus a rows dict, the untested main-process RAM risk from R21RK-3), and per-video failures that happen late in each video (e.g. CUDA OOM after the detector cache), which end in 'no video was refined'. So 'L >= base + 1.2 h -> CI ran and the v3 codes apply' does not prove CI was applied. (2) The worse false read is a spurious '+', not a '0'. A no-op exp79a is exp70g re-run, and any GPU nondeterminism could give an UP. That would drive CI stacks in W2b/W4 and a CI V_pub. The finding's wording ('never 0') covers only the '0' case. (3) The base should be the same-batch sibling exp78b (submitted 1 min earlier, knobs add about 0 runtime), not exp70g's 27 Sep latency, so that the rule controls for Kaggle-side queueing and slowdown. VALUE is small but real: this is decision hygiene only. CI's own private value is doubtful: in-sample 4-clip lab +0.0022 pooled, and the nearest transfer record is lab +0.0078 -> LB -0.002. The rule changes no score, only whether the CI lever is closed or kept, and whether a no-op is mistaken for a CI gain.
fix: Log this in CONTEXT BEFORE the exp79a submit (~00:06Z), and in any case before exp79a's first terminal header. Wording: 'CI-RAN GATE (read rule, no mechanism): for every CI file (family safetail_ci), let dL = L_hi(CI file) - L_hi(same-batch non-CI sibling). For exp79a the sibling is exp78b; if the sibling is not COMPLETE, use exp70g L_hi 7.67 h. dL <= 0.5 h -> CI NO-OP: code '?' for ANY display (+, 0 or -; a display < base still codes '-' for the file but not for the CI lever). 0.5 < dL < 1.2 h -> '?'. dL >= 1.2 h -> CI EXECUTED, and the v3 codes apply with the caveat that a late fail-soft (rewrite exception or all workers failing late) is invisible, so a CI '0' closes the lever for 28-29 Sep slot use only, not as evidence that CI = 0 on hidden data. The v rule (L_hi > 10.2 h -> ?) stands. A latency-coded NO-OP does not license a CI resubmit in W2b or W4, because a deterministic hidden-side failure would repeat: CI goes to the post-deadline list as untested.' The ledger at read time is the only input. It needs no slot, no GPU and no code change.
realistic_gain: 0 on the score (public or private). It prevents a false lever state in maybe ~5-10% of worlds (an early no-op on the hidden run) and blocks the worse error, a no-op CI read as '+' through nondeterministic noise, which would spend W2b/W4 slots on CI stacks and could put a CI file up as V_pub. It costs one CONTEXT line.
